Explain in your own words what 'Microbes in Household Food Products' refers to.
questions.a: Microorganisms like Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB) and yeasts digest or ferment dietary substrates to enhance food texture, flavor, and nutritional value.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Microbes in Household Food Products'.
questions.a: Microbial fermentation produces organic acids and gases that transform everyday food items and improve nutritional profile.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Microbes in Household Food Products', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: milk + LAB -> curd (enriched with vitamin B12)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fermented Beverages and Industrial Fermentation' refers to.
questions.a: Industrial scale production of alcoholic drinks uses yeasts to ferment fruit juices or malted cereals inside large vessels called fermentors.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fermented Beverages and Industrial Fermentation'.
questions.a: Brewer's yeast ferments carbohydrates into ethanol, giving distilled or non-distilled alcoholic beverages depending on processing.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Fermented Beverages and Industrial Fermentation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: fermentable sugars + Saccharomyces cerevisiae -> ethanol + CO2

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Antibiotics Discovery and Function' refers to.
questions.a: Antibiotics are microbial chemical secretions that inhibit growth or kill pathogenic microorganisms.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Antibiotics Discovery and Function'.
questions.a: Secondary metabolites produced by specific fungi or bacteria act as metabolic inhibitors against infectious microbes.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Antibiotics Discovery and Function', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Penicillium notatum -> Penicillin (inhibits bacterial pathogens)

concepts.title: Microbial Production of Organic Acids, Enzymes, and Bioactive Molecules

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Microbial Production of Organic Acids, Enzymes, and Bioactive Molecules' refers to.
questions.a: Specific bacterial and fungal species are cultured to yield metabolic products like organic acids, enzymes, immunosuppressants, and cholesterol-lowering agents.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Microbial Production of Organic Acids, Enzymes, and Bioactive Molecules'.
questions.a: Microbes synthesize specialized biochemicals like citric acid, streptokinase, cyclosporin A, and statins for both medical and industrial applications.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Microbial Production of Organic Acids, Enzymes, and Bioactive Molecules', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Monascus purpureus -> Statins (inhibits HMG-CoA reductase enzyme)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Primary Sewage Treatment' refers to.
questions.a: The physical separation of solid and suspended particles from municipal wastewater through both filtration and gravity sedimentation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Primary Sewage Treatment'.
questions.a: Primary treatment physically extracts floating debris and heavy grit to prepare wastewater for secondary biological treatment.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Primary Sewage Treatment', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: raw sewage -> physical filtration + sedimentation -> primary sludge + effluent

concepts.title: Secondary Sewage Treatment and Floc Formation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Secondary Sewage Treatment and Floc Formation' refers to.
questions.a: A biological process where aerobic microbes form mesh-like flocs to digest organic matter in wastewater, followed by anaerobic digestion of settled sludge.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Secondary Sewage Treatment and Floc Formation'.
questions.a: Aerobic microbial flocs consume organic pollutants in sewage, reducing water pollution before anaerobic sludge digestion.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Secondary Sewage Treatment and Floc Formation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: primary effluent + aerobic flocs + oxygen -> digested effluent + activated sludge

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Microbial Biogas Production' refers to.
questions.a: Anaerobic digestion of cellulosic agricultural waste and cattle manure by methanogenic bacteria yields inflammable biogas rich in methane.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Microbial Biogas Production'.
questions.a: Methanogens convert cellulosic animal waste into methane-rich combustible gas inside anaerobic digesters.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Microbial Biogas Production', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: cellulosic waste + Methanobacterium -> CH4 + CO2 + H2

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Microbes as Biological Control Agents' refers to.
questions.a: The deployment of biological natural enemies, parasites, or pathogens to manage pest and pathogen populations in agricultural ecosystems.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Microbes as Biological Control Agents'.
questions.a: Targeted microbial biocontrol agents suppress specific crop pests without destroying harmless beneficial insects or causing toxic chemical pollution.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Microbes as Biological Control Agents', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Bt spore ingestion -> endotoxin release in insect midgut -> caterpillar death

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Microbes as Biofertilisers' refers to.
questions.a: Living organisms like nitrogen-fixing bacteria, mycorrhizal fungi, and cyanobacteria that naturally replenish essential plant nutrients in soil.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Microbes as Biofertilisers'.
questions.a: Biofertilisers fix atmospheric nitrogen and solubilize soil phosphorus, offering a sustainable alternative to chemical fertilizers.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Microbes as Biofertilisers', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: N2 + nitrogen-fixing microbes -> organic nitrogen (plant nutrient)
